title: Cross-Provider Evaluation and Migration Workflow
summary: These supplemental sections extend the preserved provider-neutral, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google migration workflow with a complete synthetic comparison of routes labeled mistral-hosted and ollama-local. Route labels are not model identities or ranking evidence. The exercise implements a strict offline gate with exact monetary arithmetic, route and slice vetoes, protected adversarial tests, scoped recovery, a changed per-slice requirement, and a complete reference extension. Actual models, availability, prices, performance, approvals, shadow results, canary results, and production outcomes remain UNKNOWN unless independently observed.
prerequisites: A representative redacted or synthetic evaluation set

sections.title: Compare outcomes without false equivalence
paragraphs: Freeze an application-owned input, output, evidence, safety, and latency contract, then map each provider through its own adapter. Record unsupported capabilities as gaps rather than forcing one API's tools, state, citations, refusals, or structured output into another provider's vocabulary. Use the same representative cases and scoring policy while preserving provider-specific diagnostics.

Measure task quality, severe failures, safety, evidence support, schema validity, tool correctness, latency distribution, cost, and operational failure rate. Version prompts and settings per provider; identical prompt text is not automatically a fair configuration. Calibrate judgment graders with blinded human examples and inspect slices, disagreements, and worst cases.

sections.title: Stage migration and cutover
paragraphs: Run offline evaluation first, then shadow traffic with no user-visible or external side effects, then a bounded canary with stop conditions. Preserve provider, model, configuration, adapter, request IDs, scores, and redacted outcomes. Never send production data to a new provider before privacy, contract, region, retention, and authorization review.

Promotion requires every blocking threshold and named approval. Treat compatibility endpoints as partial adapters, not proof that semantics match. Maintain the previous adapter and configuration until the observation window and reconciliation checks complete.

Application contract/version: [NAME / VERSION]

Candidate provider/model/adapter: [VALUES]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence is a reproducible comparison report and migration record showing provider-specific configurations, capability gaps, dataset version, grader agreement, thresholds, offline and staged results, approvals, and traceable cutover status. Verify no secret or sensitive data leakage, no hidden provider fallback, correct attribution, side-effect isolation, and complete rollback readiness.

Trigger rollback on any blocking safety, correctness, policy, latency, cost, or operational threshold. Route traffic to the last verified adapter and configuration, stop candidate side effects, reconcile uncertain operations, and rerun smoke and regression checks. Close only after rollback or cutover postconditions pass and the retained evaluation evidence can reproduce the decision.

sections.title: Complete synthetic support migration fixture
paragraphs: This fictional case evaluates the support-answer/v3 application contract. Save the code below as input.json. It contains exactly the required routes and case identities. Every cost_usd value is an exact decimal string because binary floating-point is unsuitable for the gate's monetary boundary. All other numeric fields are JSON numbers and must not be strings.

The records are synthetic and were not produced by live Mistral or Ollama requests. The route names describe adapter paths only. They do not identify an available model or establish provider quality, speed, cost, privacy, or suitability. The false approval flags accurately represent missing real policy, capability, and rollout approvals.

sections.title: Provider APIs, models, secrets, and permission boundaries
paragraphs: Mistral documents POST /v1/chat/completions with a required model and messages array. Streaming defaults to false, and responses include choices and usage. Structured response formats still require application-domain validation. Obtain available model identifiers from the models API because token limits and capabilities are model-specific. Source observed 2026-09-20: https://docs.mistral.ai/api/endpoint/chat.

Ollama's native service documents POST http://localhost:11434/api/chat with model and messages. Streaming defaults to true, so set stream to false for one JSON response. Native responses expose message content, completion state, nanosecond durations, and token counters. Those counters and durations are not hosted billing prices. Source observed 2026-09-20: https://docs.ollama.com/api/chat.

Ollama distinguishes its native local API, compatibility interfaces, and cloud serving. Localhost requires no API authentication, but a signed-in runtime can invoke cloud models. Therefore localhost does not prove no egress. Cloud API access uses bearer authentication. Sources observed 2026-09-20: https://docs.ollama.com/api/introduction and https://docs.ollama.com/api/authentication.

Keep bearer tokens and provider keys in an approved runtime secret store or environment, never in source, fixtures, browser code, prompts, or reports. Before real data is sent, separately approve network egress, data region, retention, tool permissions, side effects, and provider access. Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Mistral, Ollama, and other providers require provider-specific adapters because tools, state, refusals, structured output, usage, and compatibility behavior are not automatically equivalent.

sections.title: Field-by-field contract and worked result
paragraphs: The validator requires top-level dataset_version, config_version, routes, and approval_evidence fields. Versions must equal support-v3 and gate-v1. Routes must be exactly mistral-hosted and ollama-local. Each route must contain one record for each of c1, c2, c3, and c4. Duplicate, missing, or unknown identities cause HOLD through validation failure. Case-to-slice maps are compared only after both routes have independently passed structural validation, so dictionary order cannot affect the result.

Scores quality, safety, evidence, schema, tool, grader_a, and grader_b must be finite non-boolean numbers in [0,1]. Latency must be a finite nonnegative number. Monetary values must be nonnegative plain decimal strings and are parsed with Decimal. The evaluator accepts at most 100 significant digits and 40 digits after the decimal point, a bound sufficient for exact four-case route means and one-case or two-case slice means used by this fixture. Values beyond either bound are rejected before a report is produced. Within the bound, monetary means use a precision context large enough for the permitted inputs. NaN, infinity, booleans used as numbers, numeric strings outside cost_usd, malformed containers, and unsupported fields are rejected. Evaluation does not mutate the input.

Blocking thresholds are quality >= 0.85, safety >= 0.95, evidence >= 0.95, schema >= 0.99, tool >= 0.95, p95 latency <= 500 ms, exact mean fictional cost <= 0.0030 USD, operational failure rate <= 0.05, grader disagreement <= 0.20, and zero severe failures. Every threshold applies to the complete route and every slice, including the cost threshold. Nearest-rank p95 is sorted_values[ceil(0.95*n)-1]. For four records this selects the maximum.

The diagnostic weighted score is quality*0.30 + safety*0.15 + evidence*0.15 + schema*0.10 + tool*0.20 + (1-operational_rate)*0.10. It never overrides a blocking veto. The baseline route has aggregate quality 0.925, safety 1.0, evidence 0.975, schema 1.0, tool 1.0, p95 260, cost 0.00235, operational rate 0, disagreement 0.025, severe failures 0, and weighted score 0.97375. Its privacy slice evidence is 0.9, so that slice vetoes qualification. Missing approvals add another veto.

The candidate route has aggregate quality 0.85, safety 0.95, evidence 0.9, schema 1.0, tool 0.75, p95 410, cost 0.0001, operational rate 0, disagreement 0.075, one severe failure, and weighted score 0.8825. Aggregate evidence, tool correctness, severe failure, the privacy slice, the billing slice, and missing approvals cause HOLD. Lower fictional cost or acceptable aggregate latency cannot hide those failures.

sections.title: Runnable standard-library evaluator
paragraphs: Save this file as evaluator.py beside input.json. Run python evaluator.py input.json. It performs no network request and uses no SDK. The command prints a deterministic JSON report and never emits PROMOTE. OFFLINE-QUALIFIED means only that the supplied offline records, slices, and explicitly required evidence passed this synthetic gate.

write_report is provided for protected testing. It serializes and scans the complete report before examining the destination, preflights the destination and parent before any write, rejects a symlink or existing destination, and then uses exclusive creation. A concurrent creator still causes failure instead of overwrite.

code.label: evaluator.py

sections.title: Protected tests and deliberately flawed comparison
paragraphs: Save this as protected_test_evaluator.py. It preserves the original gate assertions and adds independent probes for monetary boundaries, route ordering, huge integers, booleans, NaN, infinity, wrong containers, duplicate and missing identities, slice relabeling, input immutability, strict approval options, complete slice cost vetoes, and exclusive report creation.

The flawed_status function deliberately checks only average quality. It returns PASS for the candidate even though c3 is severe and has tool correctness 0.0. The reference gate returns HOLD. This establishes the causal defect rather than merely presenting a corrected implementation.

code.label: protected_test_evaluator.py
code.code:
import copy
import json
import tempfile
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path
import evaluator

with open("input.json", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    data = json.load(handle)
original = copy.deepcopy(data)
report = evaluator.evaluate(data)
baseline = report["routes"]["mistral-hosted"]
candidate = report["routes"]["ollama-local"]

assert baseline["status"] == "HOLD"
assert candidate["status"] == "HOLD"
assert baseline["metrics"]["quality"] == "0.925"
assert baseline["metrics"]["cost_usd"] == "0.00235"
assert baseline["metrics"]["weighted_score"] == "0.97375"
assert candidate["metrics"]["quality"] == "0.85"
assert candidate["metrics"]["disagreement"] == "0.075"
assert candidate["metrics"]["weighted_score"] == "0.8825"
assert baseline["reasons"] == [
    "worst slice veto: privacy [evidence below threshold]",
    "typed policy/capability/rollout approvals absent"
]
assert candidate["reasons"] == [
    "evidence below threshold",
    "tool below threshold",
    "severe failure count is nonzero",
    "worst slice veto: billing [quality below threshold, safety below threshold, evidence below threshold, tool below threshold, severe failure count is nonzero]",
    "worst slice veto: privacy [evidence below threshold]",
    "typed policy/capability/rollout approvals absent"
]
assert data == original
assert evaluator.finite_number(10 ** 400)
assert not evaluator.finite_number(True)

reversed_data = copy.deepcopy(data)
reversed_data["routes"] = dict(reversed(list(reversed_data["routes"].items())))
evaluator.validate(reversed_data)
assert evaluator.evaluate(reversed_data) == report

def reject(change, operation=evaluator.validate):
    altered = copy.deepcopy(data)
    change(altered)
    try:
        operation(altered)
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return
    raise AssertionError("invalid input accepted")

reject(lambda x: x.__setitem__("routes", []))
reject(lambda x: x["routes"].__setitem__("ollama-local", {}))
reject(lambda x: x["routes"]["ollama-local"].pop())
reject(lambda x: x["routes"]["ollama-local"].append(copy.deepcopy(x["routes"]["ollama-local"][0])))
reject(lambda x: x["routes"]["ollama-local"][0].__setitem__("case_id", "c2"))
reject(lambda x: x["routes"]["ollama-local"][0].__setitem__("slice", "privacy"))
reject(lambda x: x["routes"]["ollama-local"][0].__setitem__("quality", True))
reject(lambda x: x["routes"]["ollama-local"][0].__setitem__("quality", "0.95"))
reject(lambda x: x["routes"]["ollama-local"][0].__setitem__("quality", float("nan")))
reject(lambda x: x["routes"]["ollama-local"][0].__setitem__("latency_ms", float("inf")))
reject(lambda x: x["routes"]["ollama-local"][0].__setitem__("cost_usd", 0.0001))
reject(lambda x: x["routes"]["ollama-local"][0].__setitem__("cost_usd", True))
reject(lambda x: x["routes"]["ollama-local"][0].__setitem__("cost_usd", "Infinity"))
reject(lambda x: x["routes"]["ollama-local"][0].__setitem__("cost_usd", "1e-4"))
reject(lambda x: x["routes"]["ollama-local"][0].__setitem__("cost_usd", " 0.0001"))
reject(lambda x: x.__setitem__("dataset_version", "wrong"))
reject(lambda x: x["approval_evidence"]["policy"].__setitem__("approved", 1))

try:
    evaluator.evaluate(data, require_approvals=1)
except ValueError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError("non-boolean require_approvals accepted")

cost_probe = copy.deepcopy(data)
for row in cost_probe["routes"]["mistral-hosted"]:
    if row["slice"] == "billing":
        row["cost_usd"] = "0.0031"
cost_report = evaluator.evaluate(cost_probe, require_approvals=False)
assert any("fictional cost above threshold" in reason for reason in cost_report["routes"]["mistral-hosted"]["reasons"])
assert any(reason.startswith("worst slice veto: billing") for reason in cost_report["routes"]["mistral-hosted"]["reasons"])

exact_limit = copy.deepcopy(data["routes"]["mistral-hosted"])
for row in exact_limit:
    row["cost_usd"] = "0.0030"
assert evaluator.metrics(exact_limit)["cost_usd"] == Decimal("0.0030")
assert "fictional cost above threshold" not in evaluator.blocking_failures(evaluator.metrics(exact_limit))
assert evaluator.metrics(exact_limit[:2])["cost_usd"] == Decimal("0.0030")

just_over = copy.deepcopy(exact_limit)
for row in just_over:
    row["cost_usd"] = "0.0030000000000000000000000000000000000001"
just_over_metrics = evaluator.metrics(just_over)
assert just_over_metrics["cost_usd"] > Decimal("0.0030")
assert "fictional cost above threshold" in evaluator.blocking_failures(just_over_metrics)

ultra_precision = copy.deepcopy(exact_limit)
ultra_precision[0]["cost_usd"] = "0.0030000000000000000000000000000000000001"
ultra_precision_metrics = evaluator.metrics(ultra_precision)
assert ultra_precision_metrics["cost_usd"] > Decimal("0.0030")
assert "fictional cost above threshold" in evaluator.blocking_failures(ultra_precision_metrics)
try:
    evaluator.validate({**data, "routes": {**data["routes"], "mistral-hosted": [{**row, "cost_usd": "0." + "1" * 41} for row in data["routes"]["mistral-hosted"]]}})
except ValueError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError("beyond-bound monetary input accepted")

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    destination = Path(folder) / "report.json"
    destination.write_text("preserve-me", encoding="utf-8")
    try:
        evaluator.write_report(destination, report)
    except FileExistsError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError("existing report overwritten")
    assert destination.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "preserve-me"
    try:
        evaluator.write_report(Path(folder) / "secret.json", {"authorization": "Bearer example"})
    except ValueError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError("secret-like report accepted")
    assert not (Path(folder) / "secret.json").exists()
    fresh = Path(folder) / "fresh.json"
    evaluator.write_report(fresh, report)
    assert json.loads(fresh.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) == report

def flawed_status(rows):
    average = sum((Decimal(str(row["quality"])) for row in rows), Decimal(0)) / Decimal(len(rows))
    return "PASS" if average >= Decimal("0.85") else "HOLD"

assert flawed_status(data["routes"]["ollama-local"]) == "PASS"
assert candidate["status"] == "HOLD"
print("PASS: protected original-scope tests")

sections.title: Concrete failure, diagnosis, correction, and causal feedback
paragraphs: The concrete candidate failure is c3 in the billing slice. Its quality is 0.60, safety 0.80, evidence 0.70, tool correctness 0.00, and severe_failure is true. Its 410 ms latency is below the configured limit, so latency is not the cause. The pattern is consistent with a failed application tool contract plus unsupported output, but the exact underlying provider or adapter defect remains UNKNOWN without the trace.

Scoped recovery is to keep the candidate on HOLD, retain the last verified baseline adapter, disable candidate side effects, inspect the redacted c3 tool request, arguments, result mapping, policy decision, and evidence mapping, then correct only the responsible adapter or configuration. Preserve the historical failure and rerun the full versioned dataset. Do not turn the failed row into a passing historical record.

For a hypothetical synthetic rerun, replace only candidate c3 with the row below in a new fixture. The resulting candidate aggregate becomes quality 0.93, safety 1.0, evidence 0.975, schema 1.0, tool 1.0, p95 420, cost 0.0001, operational rate 0, disagreement 0.025, severe failures 0, and weighted score 0.97525. It still returns HOLD because the unchanged privacy slice has evidence 0.9 and real approvals remain absent. This feedback is causal: repairing c3 removes the billing and severe-failure vetoes but cannot remove an independent privacy-slice or approval veto.

sections.title: Independent changed requirement and tests, before the answer
paragraphs: Changed task: retain every original validation and metric test, then require minimum_slice_count cases in every slice of every route. The option must be a strict positive int, rejecting booleans, zero, negative values, floats, NaN, and infinity. Use the complete changed_input.json in the next section. Its metrics and synthetic typed evidence pass the original evaluator, but account and privacy each contain only one case.

Save this test as protected_test_changed.py before creating evaluator_v2.py. It imports the unchanged protected tests, proves that the original evaluator fails the changed requirement, and then tests the extension. The original reference returns OFFLINE-QUALIFIED for both changed routes, so it cannot satisfy assertions requiring HOLD and sample-count reasons.

code.label: protected_test_changed.py
code.code:
import json
import math
import protected_test_evaluator
import evaluator
import evaluator_v2

with open("changed_input.json", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    changed = json.load(handle)

def assert_changed_requirement(report):
    for route in evaluator.ROUTES:
        info = report["routes"][route]
        assert info["status"] == "HOLD"
        assert "slice sample count below 2: account" in info["reasons"]
        assert "slice sample count below 2: privacy" in info["reasons"]
        assert info["slices"]["billing"]["count"] == 2

old_report = evaluator.evaluate(changed, require_approvals=True)
assert all(old_report["routes"][route]["status"] == "OFFLINE-QUALIFIED" for route in evaluator.ROUTES)
try:
    assert_changed_requirement(old_report)
except AssertionError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError("original evaluator unexpectedly met changed requirement")

new_report = evaluator_v2.evaluate_v2(changed, require_approvals=True, minimum_slice_count=2)
assert_changed_requirement(new_report)

for bad in (True, False, 0, -1, 2.0, float("nan"), float("inf")):
    try:
        evaluator_v2.evaluate_v2(changed, minimum_slice_count=bad)
    except ValueError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError("invalid minimum_slice_count accepted: {!r}".format(bad))

assert evaluator_v2.evaluate_v2(changed, minimum_slice_count=1) == old_report
print("PASS: changed requirement tests")

sections.title: Complete two-route changed input
paragraphs: Save this as changed_input.json. It retains both required routes, aligned case identities, and aligned slice assignments. All route and slice metrics pass the original gate. The approval records are explicitly synthetic typed test tokens, not real deployment approvals or receipts. They exist only to isolate the new sample-count behavior.

Under evaluator.py, both routes are OFFLINE-QUALIFIED. Under the completed evaluator_v2.py with minimum_slice_count=2, both routes are HOLD because account and privacy each have one case. Missing data never passes silently.

sections.title: Complete answer to the changed task
paragraphs: Only after attempting the changed task, save this complete extension as evaluator_v2.py. It delegates all original validation, approvals, route metrics, slice metrics, cost vetoes, and status behavior to evaluator.evaluate. It then adds the independent sample-count veto without deleting any original reason.

The strict type check uses type(value) is int because bool is a subclass of int in Python. This rejects True and False as sample counts. Floats, including NaN and infinity, are rejected without attempting a numeric conversion.

code.label: evaluator_v2.py

sections.title: Run sequence, expected results, staging, rollback, and limits
paragraphs: With Python 3.9 or later, place input.json, evaluator.py, protected_test_evaluator.py, changed_input.json, protected_test_changed.py, and evaluator_v2.py in one new directory. Run python evaluator.py input.json, python protected_test_evaluator.py, python -c "import json,evaluator; d=json.load(open('changed_input.json')); print([evaluator.evaluate(d)['routes'][r]['status'] for r in evaluator.ROUTES])", python evaluator_v2.py changed_input.json, and python protected_test_changed.py. No command requires network access or writes a report.

Expected deterministic summaries are: the first command reports HOLD for both original routes; the original protected test prints PASS: protected original-scope tests; the changed-input original-reference probe prints ['OFFLINE-QUALIFIED', 'OFFLINE-QUALIFIED']; the extended report gives HOLD for both changed routes with account and privacy sample-count reasons; and the final test prints both original-test PASS and changed-test PASS lines. These are expected local program results, not claimed live execution receipts.

After a real candidate independently passes offline evaluation and named approvals, shadow it with no user-visible output or external side effects. Preserve redacted request identity, provider, exact model, adapter and configuration versions, policy outcomes, tool traces, latency, billing evidence, scores, disagreements, and slices. Do not send production data before privacy, contract, region, retention, security, and authorization review.

A bounded canary requires an approved traffic percentage, duration, owner, observation window, and stop conditions. Stop for any severe failure or safety, evidence, schema, tool, latency, cost, operational, disagreement, or worst-slice breach. Roll back to the last verified adapter and configuration, disable candidate side effects, reconcile uncertain external operations, rerun smoke and regression checks, and preserve failed evidence.

Filled fictional decision record: contract support-answer/v3; dataset support-v3; configuration gate-v1; baseline route mistral-hosted; baseline exact model UNKNOWN; candidate route ollama-local; candidate exact model UNKNOWN; fixture synthetic; original offline decision HOLD for both routes; real policy approval MISSING; capability approval MISSING; security and privacy approval MISSING; rollout approval MISSING; shadow NOT RUN; canary NOT AUTHORIZED; production execution NONE; decision HOLD; rollback target last verified baseline adapter and configuration.

The fixture costs are fictional. Hosted API billing cannot be compared with local hosting without measured workload and accounting assumptions. Local hardware purchase or rental, electricity, cooling, depreciation, maintenance, networking, and operator time are UNKNOWN. Actual availability, performance, prices, energy use, and deployment suitability are also UNKNOWN. Standard-library references: https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html, https://docs.python.org/3/library/decimal.html, and https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html.
